on 19 April, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 2529 of 2013
Judgement:
The appellant is 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioners and
1st respondent in M.V.O.P.No.125 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal-cum-District Judge, Chittoor.
The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claim petitioners filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- for the loss of life of Krupa Sagar in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 23.01.2007 at about 8.30 a.m. near the house of Kurralla Ramu on Sanepay-Rayachoti main road within the territorial limits of Police Station, Veeraballi.

4. The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioners are as follows:
VGKR,J On 23.01.2007 the deceased was travelling in a tractor-trailer bearing registration Nos.AP 04J 9137 and AP 04J 9138 along with his cousin and at about 8.30 a.m. when they reached the house of Kuralla Ramu on Sanepay-Rayachoti main road, the deceased fell down from the tractor-trailer due to rash and negligent driving of its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained severe bleeding injuries and succumbed to injuries while he was undergoing treatment at SVIMS Hospital,
Tirupati.
The 1st respondent is owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle and hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. The 1st respondent remained set ex parte.
The 2nd respondent/Insurance company filed a written statement by denying the manner of accident.

6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
1) Whether the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 1st respondent's tractor and trailer bearing Nos.AP 04J 9137 and AP 04J 9138?
VGKR,J

1 2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation for the death of the deceased Kurpa Sagar, if so, to what amount and from whom?

3) To what relief?
7.
During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioners, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and got marked Exs.A.1 to A.9.

On behalf of the 2nd respondent/Insurance company, R.W.1 was examined and got marked Exs.B.1 and B.2.
8.

Basing on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle and accordingly,
granted an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit against the respondents.
Aggrieved against the said order, the appellant/Insurance company preferred the present appeal.
9. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 5/claim petitioners.
VGKR,J 10.

The appellant pleaded that the Tribunal erred in fixing the liability on the Insurance company,
since the deceased was travelling in the crime vehicle, which is a goods vehicle, as an unauthorized passenger and that the policy does not cover the liability of the deceased.
11.

Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?
12. POINT:

The case of the claim petitioners is that the deceased Krupa Sagar used to earn Rs.4,000/- p.m. as a salary by doing sub- contract works and Rs.5,000/- p.m. as a milk vendor,
besides Rs.5,00,000/- p.a. from agriculture.

While the deceased was travelling in the crime vehicle driven by its driver along with his cousin and when they reached Sanepay-Rayachoti main road, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor-trailer, the deceased fell down and sustained multiple injuries and succumbed to injuries while undergoing treatment in SVIMS Hospital at Tirupati.
VGKR,J 13.
Basing on the material available on record, the learned Tribunal came to a conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor-trailer.

The evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Ex.A.1-certified copy of first information report and Ex.A.4-certified copy of charge sheet clearly proves about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor-trailer.
The Tribunal also gave the same finding.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

2 14.

sentences.text: In order to prove the quantum of compensation, the petitioners relied on the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 and also Exs.A.1 to A.9.
Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are parents and petitioner Nos.3 to 5 are unmarried brothers and sisters of the deceased Krupa Sagar.

As can be seen from the evidence of R.W.1 and so also the written statement filed by the 2nd respondent-Insurance company, the factum of the accident is not disputed by the 2nd respondent and the 2nd respondent also not disputed the fact about the legal representatives/dependents of the deceased.
VGKR,J 15.

The evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 coupled with Ex.A.3-certified copy of post-mortem certificate and Ex.A.5-certified copy of inquest report clinchingly establishes that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident in question.
I have clearly stated above that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor-trailer only.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled compensation as prayed for.

16. By considering the oral and documentary evidence, the learned Tribunal came to a conclusion that the petitioners are entitled compensation and awarded Rs.3,60,000/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.20,140/- towards medical expenses on considering Ex.A.6-medical bills, Rs.5,000/- towards transportation charges and Rs.5,000/-
towards funeral expenses.
Thus, in all the claim petitioners are entitled compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
17. As seen from the material on record, the deceased was aged about 25 years.
The Tribunal applied the multiplier "15" instead of applying the multiplier "18".
But, the claim petitioners have not filed VGKR,J any appeal by challenging the fixation of the multiplier by the Tribunal.

18. The evidence of R.W.1, who is the Administrative Officer of the 2nd respondent/Insurance company, shows that the crime vehicle was insured with the Insurance company and the policy is also on force.
As per the contention of the Insurance company, the deceased and others were travelling as unauthorized passengers in the crime vehicle and it being used for commercial purpose.

As seen from Ex.A.1-certified copy of first information report and Ex.A.8-attested copy of policy, the persons were travelling in the crime vehicle for loading and unloading purpose and the policy covers the same.
Ex.B.1 is a package policy.
As can be seen from Ex.A.1, the deceased was travelling in the tractor-trailer for loading and unloading purpose.
Therefore, the Insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner of the tractor-trailer i.e., the 1st respondent herein.
There is no dispute by the Insurance company that the driver of the crime vehicle is having a valid and effective driving licence.
VGKR,J 19.
In view of the above observations, there are no merits in the appeal and the appeal is devoid of merits and it is liable to be dismissed.
20. In the result, the appeal is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
